rulings.Rulings: [Part 2 of 2] Per Section 854 and Conservatorship of Pacheco, the court shall abate the portions of the Petition brought pursuant to Probate Code section 850 et seq until the conclusion of the civil action (see, supra, 224 Cal. App. 3d at 177). The causes of action and claims pleaded in the Petition under Probate Code section 850 et seq. (i.e. the portion of the Petition titled "Petitioner's Request for an Order Directing Transfer or Conveyance of Personal Property and for Enhanced Remedies Under Probate Code Section 850, 856, 859," beginning at 7:19 of the Petition and requests for relief under Probate Code sections 850, 856, and 859) are hereby ABATED until conclusion of the civil action, Case No. CGC-24-618593. As to the other causes of action and claims pleaded in the Petition, which are not brought pursuant to Probate Code section 850 et seq., the court has no authority to abate them under Probate Code section 854 (see, Bellows v. Bellows (2011) 196 Cal. App. 4th 505, 512-13). rulings.Case Title: 1993 ELEUTERIO GONZALEZ AND ANNA LUZ GONZALEZ REVOCABLE TRUST
rulings.Rulings: [Part 1 of 2] This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Michael B. McNaughton. Before the court is Respondent Diana Zuniga's Motion for Abatement, brought pursuant to Probate Code section 854 ("Motion"). Per the Notice of Motion, Respondent seeks abatement of Verified Petition for (1) Order Directing Transfer and Conveyance of Personal Property and for Enhanced Remedies under Probate Code [sec.] 850, 856, 859; (2) Relief from Breach of Trust (Probate Code, [sec.] 16420); (3) Financial Elder Abuse; (4) Undue Influence; (5) Imposition of Constructive Trust; (6) Declaratory Relief; and (7) Request for Accounting ("Petition"), pending the resolution of the civil action Case No. CGC-24-618593, Diana Zuniga v. Carmen A. Gonzalez, et al. The initial civil Quiet Title action was filed October 1, 2024. A Cross-Complaint was filed December 3, 2024. Petitioners Maria Candelaria and Gladys Morel filed the Petition on January 14, 2026. The Motion is GRANTED IN PART and DENIED IN PART, as follows. Under Probate Code section 854, If a civil action is pending with respect to the subject matter of a petition filed pursuant to this chapter this part and jurisdiction has been obtained in the court where the civil action is pending prior to the filing of the petition, upon request of any party to the civil action, the court shall abate the petition until the conclusion of the civil action. This section shall not apply if the court finds that the civil action was filed for the purpose of delay. The court notes, despite the statute's reference to "this chapter," part 19 of Division 2 of the Probate Code, entitled "Conveyance or Transfer of Property Claimed to Belong to Decedent or Other Person," and encompassing Sections 850 to 860, is not further subdivided into chapters. As discussed in Conservatorship of Pacheco (1990) 224 Cal. App. 3d 171, 176-178, abatement under Section 854's statutory predecessor, Section 2525, "reflects a legislative intent to dispense with the technical requirements" of the general civil abatement statute, and to promote the Probate statute's apparent purpose of avoiding duplicative actions. Abatement of a cause of action brought pursuant to Probate Code section 850 et seq. need not involve the same cause of action or the same parties in both actions. Here, abatement of the probate proceedings brought under Probate Code section 850 et seq. is sought by a party to the pending civil action, Ms. Zuniga. The pending civil action - specifically the Cross-Complaint against Ms. Zuniga - concerns the same subject matter pleaded in the Petition. Two causes of action pleaded in the Petition are brought pursuant to Probate Code 850 et seq., alleging Diana Zuniga and Carmen Gonzales wrongfully accessed and absconded with records, funds and certain financial accounts belonging to the settlors. The Cross-Complaint filed by Ms. Gonzales against Ms. Zuniga on December 3, 2024 in the related civil action pleads certain causes of action alleging Ms. Zuniga wrongfully accessed and took funds from the same or some of the same financial accounts identified in the Petition, within or around the same time period alleged in the Petition. The court finds there is common subject matter between the Cross-Complaint and the Petition. There is no showing on the papers that the civil action or cross-complaint were filed for the purpose of delay.
